title: Monkey Puzzle: Ancient Araucaria Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Chile's national tree, armoured for dinosaurs long before it reached a European square. The oldest monkey puzzles mapped so far, from Caserta to Edinburgh.
intro: Every branch of a monkey puzzle is sheathed in thick, overlapping, scale-like leaves that stay sharp for decades, an armour scientists think evolved to keep long-necked herbivorous dinosaurs from stripping the crown, tens of millions of years before Araucaria araucana ever left the volcanic slopes of central Chile and Argentina. A Cornish gardener supposedly coined the English name in the 1830s, remarking that climbing one would puzzle a monkey; Victorian Britain then planted it obsessively, which is why a grove of them can still be found guarding a Scottish castle. It is Chile's national tree and endangered in the wild, felled for timber and burned in forest fires faster than it regrows. These are the monkey puzzles mapped on the site so far, oldest first.
